data.answer:
Yes—**resident standard patent applications are concentrated in New South Wales, Victoria and Queensland**. In 2025, these states recorded 1,152, 638 and 511 applications respectively, together accounting for just over 80 per cent of resident applications, according to the Australian IP Report 2026.[1]

Concentration by volume differs from patenting intensity: in 2024, the ACT was the most patent-intensive jurisdiction, with just over 2 applications per thousand businesses, according to the Australian IP Report 2025.[2]

citations.quote: New South Wales recorded 1,152 resident standard complete applications in 2025
Queensland recorded one of the strongest increases, rising from 445 to 511 applications (+14.8%)
Together, these 3 states accounted for just over 80% of resident applications in 2025

claims.text: In 2025, NSW, Victoria and Queensland recorded 1,152, 638 and 511 resident standard patent applications respectively and together accounted for just over 80 per cent of resident applications.

citations.quote: However, the Australian Capital Territory (ACT) is the most patent-intensive, with just over 2 applications per thousand businesses in the territory (see Figure 2.7).
Figure 2.7 Patent applications by Australian states and territories, 2024

claims.text: In 2024, the ACT led on patenting intensity rather than filing volume, with just over 2 applications per thousand businesses.
